legit_paraphrase_resonanz.title: Your Diversification Is Conditional. Size It That Way.
legit_paraphrase_resonanz.content:
In July, an equity unwind ran through crowded technology and AI positions. The funds built to withstand exactly that kind of single-factor hit — diversified multi-strategy books — stilllost about 2.2% on average. Asia-Pacific equity long-short managers lost roughly 9.4%. Return streams that had looked independent for years moved together the moment leverage came down.
That is the recurring problem with how books are diversified. The correlation you write into a risk model is an average across calm and stressed periods, and the calm periods dominate the record. It flatters the book. The correlation that actually governs the portfolio in a drawdown is higher, sometimes far higher, than the one in the model.
Take the relationship most portfolios are built on. Through the low-rate years from 2009 to early 2022, US stocks and bonds ran at about−0.24. Bonds rose when equities fell, and the 60/40 earned its reputation on that. Through the 2022–23 inflation shock the correlation went to+0.64. On a three-year basis it peaked at0.66 at the end of 2024. The hedge a generation of portfolios leaned on stopped hedging, and stayed that way for years.
Source:Resonanz Capital. Anchor values: Morningstar (−0.24 in 2009–Feb 2022 vs +0.64 in 2022–23) and State Street Global Advisors (36-month reading peaking at 0.66 in Dec 2024, easing to 0.48 by Sep 2025). Path between anchor points is indicative.
2022 showed the bill. The 60/40 fell 17.5%, its worst year since 1937. Both legs lost at once: the S&P 500 was down about 18% on a total-return basis and the Bloomberg US Aggregate about 13%, the worst year in that index’s history, over the same twelve months. The ballast did nothing.
That was a slow move. The correlation drifted positive over months as inflation took over as the driver. A selloff does the same thing in days, and for different reasons.
In a sharp drawdown, three things happen at once, and each pushes correlations up.
The common point: diversification needs your positions to be reacting to different things. A large enough shock is the same thing happening to all of them.
Source:Resonanz Capital. Data: Cboe S&P 500 Implied Correlation Index (expected average correlation across index constituents); current level and historical spikes as reported by Cboe. Indicative levels.cboe.com
Equity investors can watch this directly. The Cboe Implied Correlation Index — the market’s estimate of how tightly S&P 500 names will move together — sits near 15 when conditions are calm. In the March 2020 crash it jumped to around 90. Its record is about 105. Your model assumes something like 15; the event you are protecting against runs at 90 or more.
Hold more than a handful of positions and the book’s volatility is driven mostly by the average correlation between them, not by any single position’s risk. Here is what that looks like for ten equally sized positions, each with 15% volatility, as the average correlation between them rises.
Source:Resonanz Capital. Illustrative: ten equally-weighted positions, each at 15% annualised volatility. Portfolio volatility = σ√(1/N + (1−1/N)ρ); the final column is the reduction versus holding a single position.
At zero correlation, ten positions cut volatility by roughly two-thirds. At 0.8, a normal reading in a stressed market, the reduction is under 10%. Most of the diversification you were relying on is gone in the one environment you were relying on it for.
None of this means diversification doesn’t work. It means the number you feed it is wrong. A book sized on calm-market correlation is sized for a market it will not have to survive in. Three things follow from that.
The correlation in your risk model is a calm-market number. Build the book for the one you will get when it matters, not the one you measured when it didn’t.
legit_paraphrase_resonanz.summary_en: The article argues that diversification is conditional and often fails during market stress because asset correlations, which are low in calm periods, spike dramatically during drawdowns. Standard risk models are flawed as they use long-term average correlations dominated by calm periods, thus understating true portfolio risk. This leads to oversized positions that are vulnerable when diversification benefits evaporate. The failure of the 60/40 portfolio in 2022, when the stock-bond correlation flipped from negative to strongly positive, and the surge in equity correlations during crashes are cited as key examples of this phenomenon.
legit_paraphrase_resonanz.summary_zh: 文章指出，分散化投资是“有条件的”，并且在市场承压时常常失效，因为在平静时期较低的资产相关性会在市场回撤期间急剧飙升。标准的风险模型存在缺陷，因为它们使用由平静时期主导的长期平均相关性，从而低估了真实的投资组合风险。这导致投资者头寸规模过大，在分散化效益消失时变得异常脆弱。文章以2022年股债相关性由负转为强正，导致60/40投资组合失效，以及市场崩盘时股票相关性飙升等事件作为这一现象的关键例证。
legit_paraphrase_resonanz.key_takeaway_en: Portfolios should be constructed and sized based on the high-correlation regimes experienced during market stress, not on the deceptively low average correlations that prevail in calm periods.
legit_paraphrase_resonanz.key_takeaway_zh: 投资组合的构建和规模设定应基于市场压力时期的高相关性环境，而非基于平静时期具有误导性的低平均相关性。

legit_chart_numbers_gmo.summary_en: GMO's Q2 2026 7-year forecast indicates a challenging environment for traditional U.S. assets, with U.S. Large and Small Cap Value stocks projected to have negative to zero real returns. In contrast, the highest potential returns are found in international equities, particularly International Small Value (5.4%) and Deep Value (5.9%), as well as U.S. Deep Value (4.0%), especially in a 'Low' interest rate scenario. The outlook for bonds is starkly negative, with U.S. government and inflation-linked bonds expected to yield deeply negative real returns (-6.7% and -8.1% respectively) in a low-rate environment. Emerging Market forecasts are mixed, with standard EM Value showing positive returns while EM Deep Value is negative, and both perform worse in a low-rate scenario.
legit_chart_numbers_gmo.summary_zh: GMO 2026年第二季度的7年期预测显示，美国传统资产面临充满挑战的环境，预计美国大盘和小盘价值股的实际回报为负或为零。相比之下，回报潜力最高的资产类别是国际股票，特别是国际小盘价值股（5.4%）和深度价值股（5.9%），以及美国深度价值股（4.0%），尤其是在“低”利率情景下。债券前景则极为悲观，预计在低利率环境下，美国国债和通胀挂钩债券的实际回报将出现严重负值（分别为-6.7%和-8.1%）。新兴市场的预测好坏参半，标准新兴市场价值股回报为正，而新兴市场深度价值股为负，且两者在低利率情景下表现均更差。

legit_short_teaser_robeco.title: In tune with the markets – Feeling good
legit_short_teaser_robeco.content: With a new Fed chairman settling in, markets may need to brace for choppier waters. But for now, optimism rules. AI is propelling equities higher, Korea is hitting fresh records, and Wall Street is holding firm – even celebrating the ‘greatest IP in history’, SpaceX.
legit_short_teaser_robeco.summary_en: Despite potential future volatility from a new Fed chairman, current market sentiment is highly optimistic. This optimism is fueled by an AI-driven rally in equities, record-breaking performance in the Korean market, and strong investor confidence in innovative companies like SpaceX.
legit_short_teaser_robeco.summary_zh: 尽管新任美联储主席可能带来未来波动，但当前市场情绪高度乐观。这种乐观情绪受到人工智能驱动的股市上涨、韩国市场的创纪录表现以及投资者对SpaceX等创新公司的强烈信心的推动。
legit_short_teaser_robeco.key_takeaway_en: While current market optimism, driven by themes like AI and specific market strengths, presents opportunities, investors should remain vigilant about potential monetary policy shifts from the new Fed leadership, which could introduce volatility.
legit_short_teaser_robeco.key_takeaway_zh: 尽管当前由人工智能和特定市场强势等主题驱动的市场乐观情绪带来了机会，但投资者应警惕新任美联储领导层可能带来的货币政策转变，这或将引发市场波动。
